claims.text: A WS2-based ceramic composite can provide self-lubrication over a wide temperature range.
A WS2-based ceramic composite can maintain sufficient mechanical strength for extreme mechanical systems.
The initial ceramic matrix composite contains no lubricating additives.
Protective oxide coatings enhance the high-temperature oxidation resistance of the WS2-containing composite.
The proposed composite can operate from ambient temperature to approximately 700°C under mechanical load.
Dispersed lamellar WS2 particles form lubricious shear planes within the ceramic matrix.
The ceramic matrix maintains the structural integrity of the composite.
WS2 has sufficiently low shear strength to promote sliding between its layers under mechanical stress.
Interlayer sliding in WS2 reduces friction.
The ceramic matrix supplies mechanical strength to the WS2-containing composite.
Applied oxide layers protect WS2 from oxidation.
Oxidation protection sustains WS2 lubrication at elevated temperatures.
The WS2-containing composite will have lower friction than a similar ceramic system without WS2 over a broad temperature range.
The WS2-containing composite will have lower wear than a similar ceramic system without WS2 over a broad temperature range.
A ceramic composite lacking WS2 and protective coatings will exhibit higher friction.
A ceramic composite lacking WS2 and protective coatings will wear more rapidly.
A ceramic composite lacking WS2 and protective coatings is susceptible to oxidation-related degradation at high temperature.
Exceeding the stability limits of WS2 will worsen tribological performance.
Failure of the oxide coating to prevent oxidation will worsen tribological performance.
If incorporating WS2 compromises matrix integrity, the composite's overall performance will degrade.
